title: Your Face Is the Second Password
hook: A desktop login system that only lets you in when both your password and your face match

slides.title: Your Face Is the Second Password
slides.subtitle: Master of Engineering final project, Memorial University of Newfoundland
slides.narration: This was Divyesh's master's final project! He built a login system where a password alone isn't enough: your face has to match too.

slides.title: The problem
bullets: Passwords alone can be guessed, shared or stolen
Two-factor login usually needs an extra device, like a phone for a code
A webcam is already built into most computers
The goal: combine something you know (a password) with something you are (your face)
slides.narration: Passwords can be stolen. So the idea was simple: use the webcam as a second lock that only opens for the real person.

slides.title: How it works

steps.label: Register
steps.detail: Sign up in the desktop app. The account is saved in MySQL

steps.label: Enroll
steps.detail: The webcam captures 100 face samples, saved as 200×200 grayscale images

steps.label: Verify
steps.detail: At login, the email and password are checked against the database first

steps.label: Recognise
steps.detail: A face model is trained on the user's samples and checks the live webcam feed

slides.narration: New users register and let the webcam take a hundred pictures of their face. To log in, they need the right password, and then the camera has to recognise them.

slides.title: Under the hood

steps.label: Find the face
steps.detail: OpenCV's Haar Cascade detector locates frontal faces in each webcam frame

steps.label: Describe it
steps.detail: LBPH encodes local texture patterns of the face into histograms

steps.label: Compare it
steps.detail: LBPH returns a distance score, where lower means more similar to the enrolled user

slides.narration: First the system finds the face in the picture. Then it turns the face's texture into numbers and measures how close they are to the person who signed up.

slides.title: The decision rules
bullets: Between 65 and 85 the system isn't sure, so it keeps scanning instead of guessing
LBPH is lightweight: it trains in seconds on a normal laptop CPU and copes well with lighting changes
Faces that clearly don't match are saved to an UnknownFaces folder for review
slides.narration: If the face is a close match, you're in. If it's clearly a stranger, the system takes a snapshot of the intruder. In between, it keeps looking until it's sure.

slides.title: Testing it in the real world
bullets: One registered user: their name and match score appear over their face, and the Home window opens
Two people in front of the camera: only the registered user is recognised, and the other person is labelled Unknown
Matching takes a moment: a user may briefly show as Unknown, so the system keeps scanning instead of rejecting
slides.narration: He tested it with real people. With two faces in view, it picked out the registered user and labelled the other person as unknown.

slides.title: More than a face check
bullets: Registration form with input validation and duplicate-email checks
Forgot-password flow using security questions
Desktop GUI built with Tkinter and Pillow
Each user's face samples are stored in their own folder
slides.narration: Around the face recognition, he built a complete account system, with sign-up checks and a way to reset a forgotten password.

slides.title: Limitations
bullets: No liveness check: a printed photo or a phone screen could fool the face model
Passwords are stored in plain text; a real system would hash them
The model is retrained at every login instead of once at enrollment
Accuracy drops with poor lighting, side profiles, masks or sunglasses
slides.narration: He's upfront about the limits. It's an academic prototype: a photo could trick it, and the passwords would need proper protection before real use.

slides.title: What's next, and explore it yourself
bullets: Next: switch to deep-learning face embeddings such as FaceNet or ArcFace for higher accuracy
Add liveness detection, like blink or head-movement checks, to stop photo attacks
Hash passwords and move database settings out of the code
The full code is on GitHub
slides.narration: Next steps are a smarter face model and a check that you're a real, live person. The code is on GitHub if you'd like to explore it!
